cards.front: independent variable
cards.back: What you change in a test.
cards.say: independent variable. What you change in a test.

cards.front: dependent variable
cards.back: What you measure in a test.
cards.say: dependent variable. What you measure in a test.

cards.front: control variable
cards.back: What you keep the same in a test.
cards.say: control variable. What you keep the same in a test.

cards.front: A test finds how the height of a ramp changes how far a car goes. What do you change?
cards.back: The height of the ramp.
cards.say: A test finds how the height of a ramp changes how far a car goes. What do you change? The height of the ramp.

cards.front: A test finds how the height of a ramp changes how far a car goes. What do you measure?
cards.back: How far the car goes.
cards.say: A test finds how the height of a ramp changes how far a car goes. What do you measure? How far the car goes.

cards.front: A test finds how the height of a ramp changes how far a car goes. What do you keep the same?
cards.back: The same car, the same ramp surface and the same ramp length.
cards.say: A test finds how the height of a ramp changes how far a car goes. What do you keep the same? The same car, the same ramp surface and the same ramp length.

cards.front: Why do we keep variables the same?
cards.back: So the test is fair and we can trust the results.
cards.say: Why do we keep variables the same? So the test is fair and we can trust the results.

cards.front: line graph
cards.back: A graph that joins points with a line to show how something changes.
cards.say: line graph. A graph that joins points with a line to show how something changes.

cards.front: When do we use a line graph?
cards.back: When we show how something changes over time or as we change something.
cards.say: When do we use a line graph? When we show how something changes over time or as we change something.

cards.front: What goes on the bottom (x) axis?
cards.back: What you change (the independent variable).
cards.say: What goes on the bottom (x) axis? What you change (the independent variable).

cards.front: What goes on the side (y) axis?
cards.back: What you measure (the dependent variable).
cards.say: What goes on the side (y) axis? What you measure (the dependent variable).

cards.front: What does a line going up show?
cards.back: The measured value is getting bigger.
cards.say: What does a line going up show? The measured value is getting bigger.

cards.front: What does a flat line show?
cards.back: The measured value stays the same.
cards.say: What does a flat line show? The measured value stays the same.

cards.front: What does a line going down show?
cards.back: The measured value is getting smaller.
cards.say: What does a line going down show? The measured value is getting smaller.

cards.front: trend
cards.back: The general direction the results are heading in.
cards.say: trend. The general direction the results are heading in.

cards.front: anomaly
cards.back: A result that does not fit the pattern.
cards.say: anomaly. A result that does not fit the pattern.

cards.front: What should you do with an anomalous result?
cards.back: Check it and repeat that measurement if possible.
cards.say: What should you do with an anomalous result? Check it and repeat that measurement if possible.

cards.front: conclusion
cards.back: A sentence that says what the results show.
cards.say: conclusion. A sentence that says what the results show.

cards.front: What should a conclusion refer to?
cards.back: The results and the question you asked.
cards.say: What should a conclusion refer to? The results and the question you asked.

cards.front: Why is a table useful before drawing a graph?
cards.back: It stores results in order so they are ready to plot.
cards.say: Why is a table useful before drawing a graph? It stores results in order so they are ready to plot.

cards.front: What does "the higher the ramp, the further the car goes" show?
cards.back: A pattern in the results.
cards.say: What does "the higher the ramp, the further the car goes" show? A pattern in the results.

cards.front: Which axis is labelled with units?
cards.back: Both. Label each axis with what it shows and the unit.
cards.say: Which axis is labelled with units? Both. Label each axis with what it shows and the unit.

cards.front: How can we make results more reliable?
cards.back: Repeat the test and use the average.
cards.say: How can we make results more reliable? Repeat the test and use the average.

cards.front: prediction
cards.back: What you think will happen before the test.
cards.say: prediction. What you think will happen before the test.
